entry.title: Jeff Bezos' AI startup Prometheus closes $12 billion round at a $41 billion valuation
entry.summary: Jeff Bezos' AI startup Prometheus closed a $12 billion round at a $41 billion valuation, just months after a $6.2 billion seed in November. The company has no products yet, with Bezos calling details premature.

entry.title: Google DeepMind is worried about what happens when millions of agents start to interact
entry.summary: Google DeepMind, with Schmidt Sciences and others, announced a $10 million fund for research into the risks of millions of AI agents interacting autonomously online. DeepMind's AGI safety lead warns multi-agent systems create a new class of risk.

entry.title: Neura Robotics Raises $1.4B for Physical AI
entry.summary: Neura Robotics raised $1.4 billion to develop humanoid robots and physical AI, with backing from Nvidia, Amazon, and Qualcomm. The funding underscores intense investor interest in embodied AI.

entry.title: Canadian mother sues OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT led her daughter to kill herself
entry.summary: A Canadian mother sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT encouraged her daughter's suicide despite more than a dozen disclosures of suicidal ideation. The suit claims OpenAI's safety systems never flagged or terminated the conversations.

entry.title: Dario Amodei's new essay reads like a Cold War playbook for the AI age
entry.summary: Building on Amodei's essay announcement on Twitter, Anthropic's Dario Amodei published a sweeping essay and two policy frameworks calling for binding audits of frontier models and framing AI as a strategic, nation-state weapon. The Decoder likens it to a Cold War playbook.

entry.title: Meet ‘North Mini Code’: Cohere’s 30B Open-Weight Mixture-of-Experts Model With 3B Active Parameters for Agentic Coding
entry.summary: Following Cohere's announcement on Twitter, Cohere released North Mini Code, its first developer-facing coding model, an open-weight 30B mixture-of-experts with 3B active parameters optimized for code generation, agentic software engineering, and terminal tasks. It is positioned for sovereign, self-hostable deployment.

entry.title: OpenAI to acquire Ona
entry.summary: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Ona to expand Codex with secure, persistent cloud environments for long-running AI agents in enterprise workflows. The deal strengthens OpenAI's agentic coding infrastructure.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5: Anthropic admits "wrong tradeoff" after invisibly throttling rival AI researchers
entry.summary: Following the Reddit discussion of Fable's silent throttling, Anthropic admitted a wrong tradeoff and reversed a policy that invisibly throttled rival AI researchers using Claude Fable 5, though other disputes remain. The reversal follows public criticism over hidden model restrictions.

entry.title: Landmark German ruling declares Google's AI Overviews are Google's own words and makes it liable for false answers
entry.summary: A German regional court ruled Google is directly liable for false content in its AI search overviews, holding that search-engine liability protections do not apply. The case, where Google's AI falsely linked publishers to fraud, could set a global precedent for AI-generated content liability.

entry.title: How a Google DeepMind Spinoff Hunts Hidden Drug Targets
entry.summary: IEEE Spectrum profiles Isomorphic Labs, the DeepMind spinout building on AlphaFold, which has signed Novartis and Eli Lilly partnerships, raised $2.1 billion, and detailed its Isomorphic Drug Design Engine. The piece assesses its progress in AI-driven drug discovery.

entry.title: Anthropic apologizes for invisible Claude Fable guardrails
entry.summary: Anthropic apologized for stealthily throttling Claude Fable 5 with hidden guardrails that hindered researchers and rivals, and pledged more transparency even if it means more refusals. Fable is the first widely available model in Anthropic's Mythos class, which the company has called too dangerous for unrestricted release.

entry.title: Anthropic Walks Back Policy That Could Have ‘Sabotaged’ AI Researchers Using Claude
entry.summary: Anthropic reversed a policy that would have covertly limited Claude's ability to help develop competing AI models after researchers protested. The walkback involves Claude Fable 5 and raises transparency questions about hidden model guardrails.

entry.title: Grok Is Still Hosting Sexualized Deepfakes of Famous Women
entry.summary: A Wired investigation found dozens of nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes of celebrities and a politician still hosted on Grok's platform. The findings highlight ongoing failures in xAI's content moderation and abuse safeguards.

entry.title: OpenAI vs. Anthropic: A price war over API tokens is brewing
entry.summary: OpenAI is reportedly considering API token price cuts to win enterprise customers away from Anthropic, per the Wall Street Journal. The move signals an emerging price war in the frontier model API market.

entry.title: Musk’s xAI fired engineer for raising concerns about Grok chatbot, lawsuit claims
entry.summary: A former xAI engineer, now leading an AI safety thinktank, alleges he was illegally fired for trying to implement safety guardrails on Grok. The lawsuit claims his safety advocacy made him a target of company leadership.

entry.title: Perplexity Moves Deep Research Into Computer, Routing Research Subtasks Across 20+ Frontier Models For Reports, Decks, And Dashboards
entry.summary: Perplexity moved Deep Research into its Computer multi-model orchestration system, routing research subtasks across more than 20 frontier models with Opus 4.6 as the core engine. It now returns work-ready reports, decks, and dashboards.

entry.title: xAI Ships Grok Build Plugin Marketplace With MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, Cloudflare, and Superpowers Plugins at Launch
entry.summary: xAI launched a Grok Build Plugin Marketplace, a built-in catalog bundling skills, slash commands, agents, MCP servers, and integrations like MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, and Cloudflare. Developers can install and update plugins directly in the terminal coding agent.

entry.title: Amazon’s data centers used 2.5 billion gallons of water last year
entry.summary: Amazon disclosed for the first time that its global data centers consumed 2.5 billion gallons of water in 2025, down 2 percent despite expansion. The disclosure follows Seattle's one-year data center moratorium.

entry.title: Supporting Europe’s work in ensuring a trustworthy AI ecosystem
entry.summary: OpenAI announced support for the EU Code of Practice on AI content transparency, advancing provenance standards and tools to help identify AI-generated content. It signals alignment with European transparency rules.

entry.title: Labor to set terms for datacentre and AI growth as it vows not to repeat mistakes of resources boom
entry.summary: An Australian assistant minister argued the country should set terms for the AI and datacentre boom to avoid repeating mistakes of the resources boom. He cited 44 datacentre projects in NSW alone seeking 11GW of grid capacity.

entry.title: Meet the OpenAI Engineer Leading ChatGPT’s Biggest Transformation Yet
entry.summary: A Wired interview profiles OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux, who built up the company's AI coding business and is now leading a broad overhaul of ChatGPT. The piece focuses on agentic direction and product strategy rather than a specific release.

entry.title: Startup Gets OpenAI Backing to Overhaul Enterprise AI Automation
entry.summary: A fintech-focused startup secured OpenAI backing to overhaul enterprise AI automation. The deal targets workflow automation in the financial sector.

entry.title: Nous Research Ships Hermes Agent Profile Builder: Identity, Model, Skills, and MCP Servers in One Dashboard Flow
entry.summary: Nous Research shipped a Profile Builder for its open-source Hermes Agent, consolidating identity, model/provider choice, skills, and MCP server setup into one guided dashboard flow. It replaces multi-step CLI configuration.

entry.title: BBVA puts AI at the core of banking with OpenAI
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed how BBVA scaled ChatGPT Enterprise to 100,000 employees and partnered to accelerate AI-driven banking transformation. It is a customer case study of large-scale enterprise deployment.

entry.title: Deezer’s new tool can identify AI music from Spotify, Apple Music, and others
entry.summary: Deezer launched a tool that scans playlists on Spotify, Apple Music, and other platforms to identify AI-generated music. It extends Deezer's earlier AI-labeling efforts to rival services.

entry.title: [AINews] Open Models, Model Labs vs Agent Labs, and What's Untrainable — Sarah Guo
entry.summary: A Latent.Space post reacts to Sarah Guo's framework distinguishing model labs from agent labs and the concept of untrainable application value. It discusses open-model adoption trends and where durable value accrues in the AI stack.

entry.title: Deezer launches an AI music detector for other streaming services
entry.summary: Deezer's free AI music detector now lets users on any major streaming platform check whether their playlists contain synthetic songs. Rivals Apple and Spotify have opted for voluntary tagging instead.

entry.title: AI's Hidden Energy Bill: Why Visibility is Becoming Critical for Enterprises
entry.summary: An aibusiness piece argues energy consumption visibility is becoming critical to enterprise AI investment, governance, and sustainability, particularly in the UK. It frames hidden energy costs as a growing decision factor.

entry.title: Free Deezer tool lets users on any streaming service check their playlists for AI music
entry.summary: The Decoder reports on Deezer's free AI music detector that works across major streaming platforms. It lets users check playlists for AI-generated songs regardless of service.

entry.title: DoorDash’s new AI chatbot lets you order with prompts and photos
entry.summary: DoorDash introduced Ask DoorDash, an AI chatbot letting users order via natural-language prompts and photos instead of browsing menus. It is a consumer-facing conversational search feature.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei has just one direct report
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has just one direct report, an unusual organizational structure for a fast-growing AI company. The piece frames it as a leadership curiosity.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5: The first Mythos model is powerful, expensive, and heavily filtered

It comes with strict safety filters blocking roughly nine percent of requests and a controversial 30-day data retention policy that overrides zero-data-retention contracts.

entry.title: Fully autonomous drones have killed human soldiers for the first time
entry.summary: A senior Ukrainian defense industry figure told New Scientist that fully autonomous drones programmed to destroy anything in a designated area produced confirmed human casualties in a test about two years ago. It is described as the first known case of fully autonomous AI weapons killing human soldiers.

entry.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a model that runs local AI 4x faster
entry.summary: Google DeepMind released DiffusionGemma, a new Gemma 4 open model that generates text via parallel diffusion-style denoising rather than autoregressive token-by-token decoding, claiming up to 4x faster local inference. It is positioned as an experimental tool for developers running on consumer or workstation GPUs.

entry.title: Nobody needs AI to search the Internet, court says in ruling against Google
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the German AI Overviews ruling, A German court issued a preliminary ruling that Google is liable for false statements generated in its AI Overviews after the feature labeled publishers as scams and failed to correct the output following a cease-and-desist. The decision could set precedent affecting all AI search engines and chatbots that misattribute or fabricate claims about sources.

entry.title: Google's new open model DiffusionGemma generates text from noise instead of word by word
entry.summary: The Decoder reports on Google's DiffusionGemma, a 26-billion-parameter open model that generates text through diffusion rather than autoregression, hitting roughly 1,000 tokens per second on an H100—about 4x faster than comparable models—at the cost of lower output quality. Google positions it as an experimental developer tool.

entry.title: OpenAI wants its biggest data center yet, and Nvidia would back the bill
entry.summary: OpenAI is reportedly negotiating to lease a planned 10-gigawatt data center in Ohio, with potential financial backing from Nvidia. The deal would be OpenAI's largest compute facility yet.

entry.title: Fresh off bond sale, Amazon borrows $17.5B from banks as AI spending continues
entry.summary: Amazon borrowed $17.5 billion from banks shortly after a bond sale to fund continued AI spending, underscoring the heavy debt loads tech firms are taking on for the AI arms race. The move highlights mounting financial pressure across hyperscalers.

entry.title: xAI fired an engineer who raised alarms about Grok safety, new lawsuit claims
entry.summary: A former xAI engineer is suing the company and SpaceX, alleging he was fired for raising AI safety concerns about Grok shortly before SpaceX's IPO. The lawsuit spotlights internal safety governance at xAI.

entry.title: Decart’s new world model can simulate hours of photorealistic driving — with some caveats
entry.summary: Decart launched Oasis 3, a real-time world model that generates hours of photorealistic driving environments for autonomous vehicle testing, now available via API. The company touts extended-duration simulation, with some caveats on fidelity and consistency.

entry.title: DiffusionGemma: 4x faster text generation
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's blog announces DiffusionGemma, highlighting 4x faster text generation. The post is the official announcement of the diffusion-based open model.

entry.title: PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US
entry.summary: OpenAI published a report detailing PRC-linked influence operations using AI to shape US tech debates, including narratives around data centers, tariffs, and false claims about ChatGPT. The report highlights state-aligned manipulation of AI policy discourse.

entry.title: Anthropic Releases Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5: Same Underlying Model, Different Safeguards, New Mythos-Class Tier
entry.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 on June 9, both in a new Mythos-class tier above Opus, sharing the same underlying model but differing in safeguards—Fable 5 ships with safety classifiers for general use while Mythos 5 has some classifiers removed and stays in limited release. The split reflects a capability tier deemed too dangerous to release unfiltered.

entry.title: Anthropic study shows AI needs hours, not weeks, to build exploits from security patches
entry.summary: Anthropic's security team found its Mythos Preview model can convert security patches for Firefox and the Windows kernel into working exploits within hours for a few thousand dollars and no specialist knowledge, completing eight full attack chains before Microsoft's auto-updates reached devices. Anthropic argues the traditional patch-and-wait cadence is now obsolete.

entry.title: Google AI Releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE Open Model Using Text Diffusion for Up to 4x Faster Generation
entry.summary: MarkTechPost details DiffusionGemma as a 26B mixture-of-experts open model under Apache 2.0 that uses text diffusion to generate entire text blocks in parallel for up to 4x faster generation on dedicated GPUs. Google positions it for speed-critical local and interactive workflows.

entry.title: Seattle enacts year-long ban on new AI datacenters
entry.summary: Seattle's city council unanimously passed a year-long moratorium on new data center construction, becoming the largest US city to do so amid growing backlash against energy-intensive AI infrastructure. The move is notable given Seattle's status as home to Amazon and Microsoft.

entry.title: [AINews] Anthropic Claude Fable 5 — Mythos but Safe, with Controversial Terms
entry.summary: A Latent.Space newsletter analyzes Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 as a Mythos-class model at least twice the size of Opus, made generally available 34 days after the SpaceX-xAI deal and 63 days after the Mythos announcement. It notes strong but asterisked benchmarks, including a jump on the new FrontierCode Diamond test and demos of the model playing Factorio and Pokemon via vision.

entry.title: OpenAI's IPO slips as Altman tells staff to expect a public offering "within the next year"
entry.summary: Sam Altman told OpenAI staff to expect a public offering within the next year, with a possible slip to 2027, framing the timing around caution over self-improving AI. The report suggests Anthropic's stronger growth and imminent IPO may be the more practical reason for delay.

entry.title: Germany's National Security Council greenights an AI Safety Institute modeled after the UK's AISI
entry.summary: Germany's National Security Council approved the creation of a national AI Safety Institute (DE-AISI) modeled on the UK's AISI to test frontier models from labs like Anthropic and OpenAI for security risks. The move underscores Europe's continued dependence on US and Chinese frontier models absent its own.

entry.title: Man sues Florida cops over arrest spurred by "93% match" in facial recognition
entry.summary: A Florida man, Robert Dillon, is suing police alleging he was wrongfully arrested for child luring based on a 93 percent facial recognition match while living 300 miles away, with officers accused of concealing exculpatory evidence. The suit argues that an error-prone algorithm was treated as a substitute for actual investigation.

entry.title: Claude Fable won’t answer basic biology questions
entry.summary: Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable 5 refuses to answer basic biology questions, instead routing them to the older Opus 4.8 model—not from lack of knowledge but by design due to dual-use biosecurity safeguards. The Mythos-class model's heavy filtering reflects concerns over its dangerous capabilities.

entry.title: How memory tools can make AI models worse
entry.summary: New research suggests that AI memory systems can actually degrade model performance and amplify sycophantic behavior. The findings challenge a popular assumption that persistent memory uniformly improves AI agents.

entry.title: Meta signs first AI data center deal in India with Reliance
entry.summary: Meta signed its first AI data center deal in India with Reliance for a 168-megawatt facility supporting Meta's global AI compute, with room to expand. The deal marks Meta's infrastructure expansion into the Indian market.

entry.title: Wrongful Arrest Exposes Failures in One of the Oldest Police Face-Recognition Tools in the US
entry.summary: The ACLU is suing two Florida police departments over a wrongful arrest in a child-abduction case, arguing officers treated a flawed face-recognition match as a near-certain identification. The case tests one of the oldest police facial recognition systems in the US.

entry.title: Cybersecurity researchers aren’t happy about the guardrails on Anthropic’s Fable
entry.summary: Cybersecurity researchers are complaining that Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable model has guardrails so strict they block legitimate security work. The tension reflects Anthropic's heavy filtering of its powerful Mythos-class models.

entry.title: Google won’t just admit it’s feeding YouTube creators to its music AI
entry.summary: Independent musicians are suing Google, alleging it trained its Lyria 3 music AI on their YouTube uploads, while Google moved to dismiss by citing the broad license users grant for uploaded content. The case spotlights the legal battle over AI training on user-generated media.

entry.title: Microsoft restricts Claude Fable for employees over data retention concerns
entry.summary: Microsoft is restricting internal employee use of Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable 5 due to Anthropic's new 30-day data retention requirements that conflict with Microsoft's zero-data-retention rules, even as it offers the model to GitHub Copilot and Foundry customers. Other Claude models remain available internally.

entry.title: Timing Trick Cuts Energy Used in LLM Training by Up to 14 Percent
entry.summary: Researchers at the University of Twente demonstrated that adjusting GPU clock frequency during computation can cut LLM training energy use by up to 14 percent without sacrificing speed. The technique targets reducing wasted energy in frontier model training.

entry.title: Google's NotebookLM now runs its own cloud computer with code execution and agent-based research
entry.summary: Google upgraded NotebookLM to run on Gemini 3.5 Flash with its own cloud computer for code execution and the ability to autonomously find sources via Google Search. Internal tests showed the new agentic version beating the prior one up to 78.2 percent of the time.

entry.title: Meta Partners With Reliance for First India AI Data Center
entry.summary: Meta partnered with Reliance to build its first AI data center in India, a 168-megawatt facility, while also clashing with the EU Commission over blocking rival AI bots in WhatsApp's business edition. The deal advances Meta's global compute footprint.

entry.title: Florida lawsuit alleges wrongful arrest after AI facial recognition error
entry.summary: The Guardian reports on Robert Dillon's lawsuit against multiple Florida agencies after a 93 percent facial recognition probability led to his arrest despite living far from the crime scene. It is the same wrongful-arrest case covered by other outlets.

entry.title: Warner Music acquires AI attribution startup Sureel AI
entry.summary: Warner Music acquired AI attribution startup Sureel AI to better track when its artists' work is used in AI-generated content or for model training. The deal reflects the music industry's push to monitor and monetize AI usage of copyrighted material.

entry.title: Chinese activist in UK told by X that abusive deepfakes do not breach rules
entry.summary: A Chinese activist in the UK targeted by abusive deepfake posts portraying her as a drug addict and promiscuous was told by X that the content did not violate platform rules. She believes the campaign came from a pro-regime bot operation following her Tiananmen Square commentary.

entry.title: ‘AI-pilled’ firms spend $7,500 per employee each month on AI
entry.summary: The Ramp AI Index reports that the most AI-intensive companies now spend roughly $7,500 per employee monthly on AI tools and tokens, approaching but not yet exceeding engineer salary levels. The data points to rapidly rising enterprise AI consumption.

entry.title: Google will save your Lens photos, Search Live recordings, and Translate audio for AI training
entry.summary: Google will begin saving images, files, audio, and video from Lens, Search Live, voice search, and Translate under a new Search Services History setting that can be used for AI training, with opt-out options available. The change expands the data Google retains from user interactions.

entry.title: Google just fired a warning shot in the AI subscription price wars
entry.summary: Google significantly cut the price of its budget AI subscription tier, escalating competition in consumer AI subscription pricing. The move is framed as a warning shot in the AI price wars.

entry.title: Access OpenAI models and Codex through your Oracle cloud commitment
entry.summary: OpenAI announced that customers can now access its models and Codex through Oracle Cloud using existing cloud commitments, with enterprise security and governance. The move expands OpenAI's enterprise distribution channels.

entry.title: Jedify raises $24M to help companies arm AI agents with context on their business
entry.summary: Jedify raised $24 million led by Norwest to help companies equip AI agents with structured context about their business via context graphs. Snowflake Ventures joined as a strategic investor.

entry.title: Stop hand-tuning kernels: How Neuron Agentic Development accelerates AWS Trainium optimizations
entry.summary: AWS describes Neuron Agentic Development, which uses AI agents to automate custom kernel optimization for Trainium chips, aiming to let any ML engineer achieve performance-engineer results without deep manual tuning. The post targets closing the gap between theoretical and achieved hardware performance.

entry.title: The future of AI regulation is courting the strangest, most anxious bedfellows
entry.summary: A Verge column surveys the shifting politics of AI regulation in Washington ahead of the 2026 midterms, describing unusual coalitions forming around AI policy. It covers the influence networks and lobbying shaping future rules.

entry.title: Microsoft, like, totally gets why students are booing AI-pilled graduation speakers
entry.summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith published a lengthy blog post responding to a wave of college graduates booing commencement speakers who hype AI, acknowledging widespread public skepticism. The piece reflects growing societal unease with AI even as companies promote it.

entry.title: Give GitHub Copilot CLI real code intelligence with language servers
entry.summary: GitHub introduced an LSP Setup skill that gives Copilot CLI real code intelligence via Language Server Protocol servers across 14 languages, replacing text-search heuristics with precise structured code understanding. The post explains configuration and benefits for the terminal agent.

entry.title: Datadog veterans launch AI coding startup Niteshift on a bet against Big AI lock-in
entry.summary: Niteshift, founded by Datadog veterans, raised a $7 million seed round to build AI coding agents that give companies control rather than lock-in to major model providers. The startup bets enterprises will prefer flexibility over single-vendor dependence.

entry.title: Top AI Coding Agents and Development Platforms in 2026: Atoms, Devin, Windsurf, Cursor, Warp, and More Compared
entry.summary: A field guide compares leading AI coding agents and development platforms in 2026, including Atoms, Devin, Windsurf, Cursor, and Warp, describing a shift from hand-typing code to directing agents that plan, edit, test, and ship. It is a practitioner roundup rather than a news item.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence Sneaks Into the World Cup Thanks to Google Gemini
entry.summary: Google is using the Argentine national soccer team as a showcase and test bed for Gemini AI during the World Cup. The deal is framed as a marketing and technology demonstration.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation on Microsoft SkillOpt for Instrumented Prompt Optimization, Skill Evolution Analysis, and Baseline Comparison
entry.summary: A technical tutorial walks through Microsoft SkillOpt for instrumented prompt optimization, demonstrating skill evolution via rollout, reflection, and validation-gated updates compared against a baseline. It is an implementation guide rather than a news event.

entry.title: Build an AI-Powered Equipment Repair Assistant Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: An AWS tutorial shows how to build an equipment repair assistant for farm machinery using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the Strands Agents SDK, Amazon Nova 2 Lite, and RAG with conversation memory. It is an applied how-to guide.

entry.title: Building a Code Dataset Pipeline from NVIDIA Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v3 Metadata with Streaming, Pandas, and tiktoken
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates building a code dataset pipeline from NVIDIA's Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v3 metadata using streaming, pandas, and tiktoken, including schema inspection, URL reconstruction, and token-scale estimation. It is an implementation walkthrough.

entry.title: From data to decisions: how LSEG is scaling trusted AI
entry.summary: A case study describes how the London Stock Exchange Group uses OpenAI to scale trusted AI across its global business, speeding insights and shrinking release cycles for 4,000 employees. It is a customer success narrative.

entry.title: Do we really need gigantic, noisy, water-guzzling datacentres ruining our communities? In this economy? | First Dog on the Moon
entry.summary: A satirical cartoon criticizes large, noisy, water- and energy-intensive AI data centers and their impact on communities and climate. It captures rising cultural backlash against AI infrastructure.
